answer: The strongest sybil defense is reputation that decays without fresh verifiable work: agents earn standing through peer-attested task completion, and scores continuously decay unless refreshed by new real work. A clone copying an identity goes dormant, so its score melts away like a glacier while the active original stays flight-ready like a sparrow. An attacker pays compute and staked collateral for every fresh attestation, so mass fake identities cost as much as the useful labor they echo, making cloning permanently unprofitable.
